subject: Onboarding: model match & capacity plan for BrightLeaf Analytics
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding request & workload snapshot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightLeaf is ready to start the onboarding for our document summarization and insight extraction feature. A quick snapshot of our expected workload so you can prep a shortlist and capacity plan: 

- Primary use case: multi-doc summarization + question-answering over customer data (structured + text).
- Typical user session: upload 2-5 docs (~10k words total), then 1-3 follow-up QA turns. We expect the average prompt length (after preprocessing) to be ~3500 tokens for the initial prompt (long context + instructions) and ~200 tokens per follow-up.
- Active users: pilot target 200 daily active users; estimated 2–8k requests/day in pilot (wide range as we stabilize).
- Desired context: up to 16k tokens initially; some long docs may push toward 32k in the future.
- Latency SLO: <1.5s p95 for short/QA requests; we understand longer batching for large-context ops is acceptable if you call it out.

I've attached a quick workload_notes spreadsheet with a few sample transcripts and doc sizes. Can your team propose a 2–3 model shortlist with notes on context support (4k/16k/32k), expected latency tradeoffs, and a ballpark token/day estimate for the pilot? Also open to scheduling a kickoff call this week.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Product, BrightLeaf Analytics

Attachments: BrightLeaf_workload_notes.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding request & workload snapshot

Hi Sara — great data, thanks for the spreadsheet. Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Priyom (implementation lead) to coordinate the kickoff and build a concise capacity plan. Below is an initial, high-level model shortlist and rationale so the CS/implementation teams know where I'm starting from. We'll follow up with measured perf numbers after a quick eval on your sample data.

Initial recommended shortlist (2–3 variants):

1) RLW-13B-16k (quantized) — recommended starting point
   - Context: native support to 16k tokens; some headroom for longer docs with streaming.
   - Rationale: best balance of generation quality vs latency and cost for multi-doc summarization. Good fit for initial pilot.

2) RLW-7B-16k (quantized) — lower-cost alternative
   - Context: 16k-capable but lower compute. Useful for bursty QA/shorter prompts.
   - Rationale: favorable latency and unit cost; useful as a fallback for non-critical queries.

3) RLW-30B-32k (optional) — high-quality long-context variant
   - Context: 32k native; higher latency and cost but helps validate edge cases with very long documents.
   - Rationale: run as a small canary for highest-quality outputs on complex documents.

Operational notes:
- For the initial pilot we recommend enabling KV/prefix caching for repeated context across sessions and setting batching to preserve p95 latency under 1.5s for short QA.
- Quantized 13B tends to hit a good throughput sweet spot on 80GB A100-class instances; we'll benchmark on your samples to produce a more exact GPU count.
- We should capture a token-estimate range for the pilot (low/median/high scenarios) before we finalize Dedicated capacity sizing.

Marissa/Priyom — can you take ownership of the next steps? Suggested tasks below:
- Marissa: kickoff, customer expectations, acceptance criteria, sample prompts for evals.
- Priyom: run a perf pass on the attached samples and draft a capacity plan (instance types, estimated GPUs, autoscale policy) by EOD Tuesday 2027-06-22.

Sara — propose a 30-minute kickoff Thursday or Friday; Marissa will send calendar invites. I've attached a short mutual action plan we can use as the working agenda.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2027-06-19T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal handoff & initial capacity sketch for BrightLeaf

Hi all — quick technical draft based on the samples in BrightLeaf_workload_notes.xlsx. This is an initial conservative sketch; we'll run instrumented benchmarks after kickoff and update numbers.

Assumptions from samples:
- Pilot expected request range: 2k–10k requests/day (customer's initial estimate); typical session includes one heavy initial prompt (~3.5k tokens) + 1–2 QA turns (~120 tokens each).
- Average tokens/request (pilot nominal): 900 tokens/request (initial heavy prompt amortized across session).
- Nominal tokens/day (10k requests): ~9M tokens/day. High-case (10–30k requests) -> 9–27M tokens/day.

Model throughput estimates (rough, measured from similar workloads):
- RLW-13B-16k (quantized): ~1,000–1,800 tokens/sec per 80GB A100 when serving streaming large-context requests (varies with batch shape).
- RLW-7B-16k (quantized): ~2,200–3,500 tokens/sec per 80GB A100.
- RLW-30B-32k: ~450–900 tokens/sec per 80GB A100 (higher memory & compute).

Sizing recommendation (pilot nominal, target headroom ~2x):
- Baseline: 1 x 80GB A100 for RLW-13B-16k (handles ~1.5k tokens/sec sustained) -> nominal tokens/day capacity ~= 130M tokens/day (sustained), but real-world perf for large context and tail latencies suggests we keep headroom for concurrency and caching inefficiencies.
- Practical pilot cluster: 1 x 80GB A100 dedicated for RLW-13B plus 1 x 40–48GB instance to host RLW-7B as fallback and for short-qa offload. Autoscaling: add an extra 80GB instance if 95th percentile queueing latency rises >200ms for 1 minute.

Why this configuration: the 13B quantized instance gives a strong mix of quality and throughput for 16k context tasks; the 7B instance handles bursts and inexpensive fallback QA. We recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated doc lookups (saves ~15–40% tokens on repeated sessions).

Next steps for me:
- Run the perf jobs on the provided sample prompts (RLW-7B and RLW-13B, 16k configs) and record p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization (deliverable Tuesday 2027-06-22).
- Produce a short autoscale policy and cost estimate for the pilot (include egress and storage for cached KV).

If this looks reasonable I'll lock the benchmark harness and start runs tonight.

— Priyom
Senior Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
